body: Star Wars Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader is Factor 5 and LucasArts' GameCube flying game, following Luke Skywalker and Wedge Antilles through battles associated with the original film trilogy. Released alongside the console in North America, it turns familiar spacecraft and locations into directly controlled missions. Attacking a target, defending an ally or finding an opening through a larger battle gives each sortie its immediate purpose. The player recognises the spectacle from the films, then has to understand which part of it the current craft is expected to change.

The command cross lets the player give limited instructions to supporting pilots while concentrating on the craft under direct control. Different ships have their own weapons, speed and handling, making the mission's objective important to choosing an approach. Completing a level opens the possibility of returning with other available craft. Hidden upgrades improve eligible ships, adding another reason to inspect the surroundings during a replay. The next useful discovery may be somewhere away from the most obvious line toward the current target.

Completion time, accuracy, destroyed enemies, protected allies and other measures determine the medal awarded after a mission. Meeting the stronger requirements means learning the operation as a connected sequence rather than simply reaching its conclusion. Chris Hülsbeck's score works with John Williams's familiar themes to support that cinematic scale. Rogue Leader became an early demonstration of the GameCube's capabilities, but its repeated appeal rests on the player finding a clearer, more reliable way through a battle that initially seemed overwhelming.
